## Overview

LRPMM102 is the **focal-slope prior-sensitivity companion** to
[LRPMM02](../lrp-rli-mm-002/), the errors-in-variables code→word-reading mechanism. It is
the same model, the same data and the same sampler settings, differing in exactly one
thing: the prior on the **focal** structural slope.

| | LRPMM02 (reference) | LRPMM102 (this model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focal slope $\beta_{\text{code}}$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 1)$ |
| arm covariate $\beta_G$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ — unchanged |
| all other slopes (age, HS, SP, RW, missingness) | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ — unchanged |
| everything else | — | identical, including `target_accept` = 0.999 |

## Why this model exists

The prior-critical review (#382) flagged the LRPMM02 code→word slope as the one place in
the suite where a headline prior is plausibly **under-scaled**. `N(0, 0.3)` is the
association-scale default every adjusted covariate takes — but the code→word slope is
the suite's documented **primary mechanism**, and the linear mechanism factory prices
that role at `N(0, 1)`. An earlier draft of the review read LRPMM02's upper interval
limit as "pressing against a prior ceiling"; that reasoning was corrected (a Normal
prior is unbounded, so an interval ending near two prior SDs is not ceiling evidence) —
which left the honest position that the attenuation question was simply **untested**:
the only registered sensitivity companion (LRPMM101) varies the measurement-layer
priors, never the structural slope.

$\beta_G$ and the covariate/precision slopes deliberately keep the association scale:
the review's recommendation 1 widens the mechanism slope only ("do **not** rescale
`beta_G`: it is a correctly-scaled association covariate"), and widening the whole set
would confound the answer.

## How to read the comparison

The two fits may be compared only when both current reporting traces pass the complete
automatic gate. If the LRPMM02 posterior is genuinely data-dominated, the slope here
should match it to within Monte-Carlo error. A materially larger slope under the wider
prior means the reported estimate is prior-attenuated — the association scale doing
quiet work — and LRPMM02's interval should then be read as conservative, with this
fit's interval quoted beside it.

_Measurement / triangulation, NOT causal._ As with LRPMM02: per the locked DAG's
**ID-2** the code→W slope is a latent-ability-confounded **adjusted association**, and
$\beta_G$ is an adjusted-association covariate, not the available-case modified ITT estimate (that
lives in [`lrp-rli-itt-010`](../lrp-rli-itt-010/)).
